key: In the next age they loved them and praised them. In the next they feared them; in the next they despised them.
s: Tracing rule from the highest antiquity, the chapter names three later ages; Wang Bi, on chapter 17, takes them as lesser rulers: one who, unable to govern by non-action, bestows favours, one who relies on power, and one who rules by cleverness and is evaded.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 17, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

evidence.words: 不能以無為居事，不言為教，立善行施，使下得親而譽之也。…不復能以恩仁令物，而賴威權也。…不能法以正齊民，而以智治國，下知避之，其令不從
evidence.gloss: Unable to abide in affairs by non-action and to teach without words, he sets up goodness and dispenses favours, so that those below come to love and praise him. … No longer able to command things by kindness and benevolence, he relies on majesty and power. … Unable to order the people by correct law, he governs the state by cleverness; those below learn to evade him and his orders are not followed.

reason: The problem holds: the old sentence ran to 57 words and its plain sense restated the key verse. Rewritten to rules 1 and 2: the plain sense now gives context only (the chapter traces rule down from the highest antiquity and the verse names the three later ages) and repeats no four-word run of the key; the reading is Wang Bi's, shortened, each ruler carried by his comment on the matching line, re-read in packet.js tao 17 (不能以無為居事…立善行施; 賴威權; 以智治國，下知避之). 'Is evaded' compresses 下知避之; the clause on orders not followed is dropped for length, not changed. Key, ref, at, commentator, src and evidence unchanged. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 17, at [16]); entry-check ok, 45 words.
